title: Have u made money out of it ?
author: moabdelw
selftext: I have a game theory for a solid mobile game ,so I'm starting to learn unity and I'm going to be using claude code for the whole coding , I understand it's not easy so I'm asking if someone actually made money out of an AI coded game here ?

comments.author: Shalke97
comments.body: I Made grim reach Idle on Steam and Just Sold my 600th unit in Steam. But i cannot recommend Mobile Games/Apps as The Market for that is far more brutal.

comments.author: __SlimeQ__
comments.body: bro (almost) nobody makes money with games, you're gonna make even less money with a vibe coded game. seek profits elsewhere

replies.author: moabdelw
replies.body: Even if the game is solid and has cool gameplay ?

replies.author: nievinny
replies.body:
More then 80% make no money at all. And it do not matter if you use ai or not.
If you add to that that developing a game solo can take years. It's very brutal market.

And this is not to disencourage you, some still make it, but if you want to make quick buck doing games that is the worst market to try.

replies.author: aicis
replies.body:
Yes, but also 80% of games are pure garbage.
I have yet to see any decent game without sales.

replies.author: __SlimeQ__
replies.body: steam doesn't show you the decent games without sales. and it also doesn't tell you how many sales were made and steamspy is wildly inaccurate when low numbers are involved. you can't actually draw any meaningful conclusions until you see the backend for a real game

replies.author: aicis
replies.body:
We can infer from reviews. There are databases that are available with this info.

People say this all the time and we have all the data needed to prove me wrong, yet no one can.

Feel free to try, find a single good game without any reviews and prove me wrong.

replies.author: __SlimeQ__
replies.body:
i'm not going to go play every game i can't find on steam to prove you wrong. sorry. my point is this is a circular definition. garbage games are the games without sales, games without sales are garbage games.

but if you release a game and slip through the cracks and leave the launch window without enough sales/reviews for whatever reason (price, bad store page, bad trailer, controversy, bugs, refunds, whatever), you're just not going to be promoted anymore. and steamspy will say you're at "0...20,000" sales when you're actually sitting at like 100. they're guessing, and if you make any decisions based on their numbers you are gonna have a wildly inflated sense of how much money other people are making with small "garbage" games. they are not, and your "garbage" game will not either

replies.author: aicis
replies.body:
I was specifically talking about games with no sales all.

Of course there are a lot of factors about how many sales you get (once you do get them).

But it is also extremely unlikely to flop with a good game. Only if the budget was inadequate for the scope.

replies.author: __SlimeQ__
replies.body:
i generally agree that it's unlikely and the standard on the marketplace is low.

i don't think the person you were responding to meant literally $0, they mean no money as in not something significant enough to matter. if you drop hot garbage on steam you'll still probably get a few bites just from being on the new releases list. you might make like a dozen sales and get 3 reviews or something.

sure that means you made maybe 70 dollars but if you put more than 70 hours into it (which you most likely did) you might as well have made $0. and if you consider the opportunity cost of spending 1000 hours developing a garbage game full time instead of working, you're actually just hemorrhaging money.

replies.author: Shalke97
replies.body:
Dont listen to them. You just have to find a genre where vibe coding is possible. Everything 2D is good. I am already working on my second Game which is a Tower defense Game. All assets can easily be generated with Codex, i use The CLI to get perfekt chroma Key results. 
I spent roughly 2 months until i released my game to early Access but it is important to have an Idea about Games and their Design, have a Goal in mind, define your 1.0 Version and just give it a try. Make sure to Set Up your steamworks Account rather sooner than later. And be aware that you need the proper Tools. Im using Claude to Code, 180€ monthly. And Codex for Art and mockups, 120€ monthly. The First months are an Investment but its a Grind. Im currently sitting at around 2000€ net profit after 6 weeks. Dont get advice here on Reddit, people will Always drag you down. Just Look at your Goal and start.

comments.author: RickRelentless
comments.body: Game dev is something masochistic people do out of passion. It requires crazy time investment and for the vast majority never returns any profit. It is literally the worst ‘side hustle’ you could come up with if making money is your goal. You’d be statistically better off working in a bar or fast food joint on the weekends. So ask yourself this: “Would I’d consider my time well spent, if I’d work for months/years on a game, even if it ends up with virtually no sales?” If the answer is “no, then don’t even bother.

comments.author: Kosh_Ascadian
comments.body:
AI in coding for gamedev is another tool to use. It's a pointless specifier for such a question. It's about like going on a graphical design forum for photoshop users and asking if anyone has made money out of designing things in photoshop. Why add the specifics, they don't give you any extra info. Just ask gamedevelopers overall how its making games in 2026.

So question is do people make money building games:

Yes they do. I'm one of them (haven't used AI for a single thing I've shipped tho to be clear).

But... it's a brutal industry full of extreme competition and any euro earned comes very difficult. Making the game is only 1/2 the work as well. Marketing and getting it in front of people is just as much work all over again.

If you're from a place where a low income goes far and you're already very interested in games and you already have skills in yhe field: There's a possibility to make some money.

If you're from anywhere else, not into gamedev just in it for the money, starting at complete zero etc: Look pretty much anywhere else.

comments.author: Nasilbitatbirakti
comments.body: Coding the game with AI has no effect on whether or not it's gonna make money. On mobile it's very difficult to make money via ads. 10 years ago I made a game on mobile which hit close 100k downloads and it only made a couple hundred bucks. If I were to make a mobile game I'd make sure to include in game purchasables. That way even if you get a thousand players and they make 1$ in game purchase on average you'd make more than what you'd make via ads on 100k downloads.

comments.author: jazzuoDOTcom
comments.body: Why it makes no money? And what about getting some gigs based on portfolio?

comments.author: imnotabot303
comments.body:
People don't get into indie game dev to make money, they do it as a hobby and passion project and a miniscule amount of them get lucky by making good games or going viral.

Game dev isn't a space to choose if your goal is making money. On top of that as AI improves it's going to become easier and easier for people to flood the market with games and so over time it will just become more difficult to even get your game seen let alone make money.

As AI improves we will eventually reach a point where if you can make a game without any game dev skills, so can everyone else so why will they then pay for yours.

replies.author: emperormarkus
replies.body:
Is very true. Somebody will make a little money but most of us do it for fun. That’s ok, too.

I think you have to manage your own expectations. The barriers to entry have gone because of AI and tech as a whole. That makes it harder to break out of the pack.

I am having a blast and feel the money that goes out the door is well spent.
